All expected files are in place, and `ios/`, `.expo/`, and the podspec-generated `modules/expo-speech/ios/assets/` copy stay untracked per `.gitignore`.

## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md §5 (Transcribe/Speech):

- **`modules/expo-speech/`** — new local Expo module wrapping `Speech`/`SFSpeechRecognizer` (iOS-only, scaffolded with `create-expo-module` then trimmed to match `expo-health`'s shape). Bundles `spec-assets/sample.wav` into the app via a CocoaPods resource bundle — since CocoaPods can't glob resources outside a pod's own root, the podspec uses a `prepare_command` to copy the file in at `pod install` time (untracked, gitignored).
- **`screens/TranscribeScreen.tsx`** — wired to the module: authorization status/request, live-streaming partial transcript via `onPartialTranscript` events, final transcript with a `Completed in N.N s` line timed in JS, and error text in the status line on failure.
- **`app.json`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`.

Along the way I fixed a real bug: the legacy `promise.reject(code, message)` two-arg form in this expo-modules-core version always surfaces `"undefined reason"` to JS (its `reason` never consults the passed description) — replaced with a `LocalizedError` struct rejected via `promise.reject(error)`, which correctly propagates the message. I also set `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = false` and `taskHint = .dictation` for correctness.

Full build (`prebuild` + `xcodebuild`) succeeds cleanly. At runtime, permission grant/deny and the UI flow all work correctly, but actual transcription fails in this Simulator/host environment — traced via system logs to Apple's on-device Siri speech model asset failing to install (a broken Cryptex-packaged asset, reproduced identically on a brand-new never-used simulator device too), which is an environment/infrastructure limitation, not an app defect. On that failure the app behaves exactly per spec: error text in the status line, button re-enables, no crash.
